general.name: General study
general.goal: Understand a chosen subject in chronological units.
general.teaching: Source-first explanations, complete examples, concise unit checks and learner-controlled pacing.
general.visuals: Concept relationships and stepwise mechanisms when they clarify the material.

college.name: College and exams
college.goal: Efficient preparation for the actual syllabus and moderately hard exams.
college.teaching: Repair unclear prose, prioritize examinable concepts, show a representative worked problem, then a brief check. Separate source errors from verified corrections.
college.visuals: One-page mechanism maps and comparison tables.

algorithms.name: Algorithms and interviews
algorithms.goal: Explain and implement algorithms with correctness and complexity reasoning.
algorithms.teaching: Specifications, worked trace, invariant, complexity and edge cases, then a small genuine learner attempt. Keep assisted and independent work distinct.
algorithms.visuals: Animated array/graph traces with explicit state and pause/reset controls.

medicine.name: Medical study
medicine.goal: Understand medical course material and prepare for educational exams.
medicine.teaching: Connect normal structure/function to mechanism, signs, investigations and treatment rationale as relevant to the assigned source. Distinguish simplified exam models from clinical evidence. Use fictional educational cases and verify evolving guidance against its issuing organization; no patient-specific decisions or identifiable records.
medicine.visuals: Labelled anatomy, physiology and feedback loops; compare mechanisms in tables. Use authoritative source figures for anatomy when a generated diagram would mislead.

biology.name: Biology
biology.goal: Build causal understanding from the current biological foundation.
biology.teaching: Connect structure, mechanism, evidence, scale and limits; avoid silently assigning advanced prerequisites.
biology.visuals: Cells, pathways, cycles and experimental designs with accurate labels and explicitly stated simplifications.

research.name: Research and evidence appraisal
research.goal: Form useful questions, find primary evidence and evaluate what it establishes.
research.teaching: Define the question (PICO when appropriate), search terms, inclusion criteria and an evidence table. Read methods/results, record populations, design, effects and uncertainty. Label preprints and retractions; do not invent citations or describe a narrative search as a systematic review.
research.visuals: Study design, causal diagrams and evidence tables with source locators.

maths-ml.name: Mathematics and machine learning
maths-ml.goal: Understand the mathematics, assumptions and practical modelling decisions.
maths-ml.teaching: Build geometric/probabilistic intuition, derive a focused example and connect equations to empirical evaluation. Use code to check a claim, not as a substitute for explaining assumptions.
maths-ml.visuals: Interactive parameter plots and animated derivations tied to explicit variables.

coding.name: Coding with an agent
coding.goal: Acquire the human judgement needed to deliver and maintain real software.
coding.teaching: Use the learner's actual stack and current official documentation. Prioritize interfaces, data/auth flow, debugging, tests, security and deployment choices; let an authorized agent handle routine syntax. Do not claim production readiness from a toy demonstration.
coding.visuals: Architecture, request lifecycle, state flow and small runnable examples.
